_note: Adding a population estimate is a data commit, not a code change: run app/etl/masque_population_etl.R, commit the JSON it writes into this folder, and add its path here. app/population.html validates each listed file against app/etl/population_estimates.schema.json before rendering it and refuses anything that fails. Paths are relative to app/. One artifact per survey cycle (plus an age-restricted comparator where noted); cycles and surveys are not pooled.

reviewed.reason: No headache item: the NHIS pain module, which carries PAIHDFC3M_A, is fielded in odd years only. The phenotype requires the headache arm, so no estimate is possible for this year.
reviewed.wouldChange: Nothing in this file; use the adjacent odd-year cycles.

reviewed.reason: No headache item, for the same reason as 2020.
reviewed.wouldChange: Nothing in this file; use the adjacent odd-year cycles.

reviewed.reason: The extract (445,200 adults, 72 of the survey's columns) keeps the weight _LLCPWT but drops the stratum _STSTR and PSU _PSU, so no design-based interval can be computed. BRFSS 2022 also has no headache, dizziness or tinnitus item; the only ear item is DEAF (serious difficulty hearing). The extract codes 'not asked' as 0 (DEAF = 0 for 18,644 adults), which would read as a negative answer.
reviewed.wouldChange: The full LLCP2022 file would restore the design and the blanks, but still could not express the phenotype: it would support a hearing-difficulty component estimate only.

reviewed.reason: The public-use files are fixed-width text with no column names or positions, so diagnoses, reasons for visit, weights (PATWT) and design variables (CSTRATM, CPSUM) cannot be located without the NCHS record layout. NAMCS counts physician office visits, not people: an estimate would be a share of visits, not a population prevalence.
reviewed.wouldChange: The NCHS layout for each year (the SAS or Stata input program, or the Stata .dta release of the same files). NAMCS diagnosis codes would also make the sinonasal arm expressible for the first time.
